messages:
Maria P.: quick follow-up from the RFC yesterday — can we support a per-request 'precision-gradient' that adapts FP8 -> INT8 -> 4bit inside a single response? thinking of prompt segments that need higher fidelity vs cheap token tails.

Chris W.: interesting. main concerns: kernel jump cost, KV cache compatibility, and how we measure when to step down.

Liam T.: +1 to kernel cost. also cache warming: switching precision mid-sequence might invalidate cached kv for that slice unless we normalize.

Sasha R.: we prototyped something similar in perf experiments (local). Two findings: 1) switching only at block boundaries (every 64 tokens) limits churn. 2) quality drop is concentrated on tokens where attention distribution shifts.

Maria P.: good — so block-aligned switches are a reasonable constraint. how do we decide switches? heuristics vs learned?

Chris W.: propose a hybrid: cheap heuristic (e.g., perplexity slope, token-level SNR) to trigger candidate switch, then lightweight classifier (offline-trained) to accept/reject. keeps runtime cheap.

Liam T.: classifier needs features that are cheap to compute on the critical path. e.g., logits entropy, max-prob diff, recent KV norm. all O(vocab) or O(1) approximations?

Sasha R.: we measured entropy and a moving-window logit variance — both correlate with perceived quality regressions. attaching gist of the tiny config we used: 
```json
{
  "precision_gradient": ["fp8","int8","4bit"],
  "block_size": 64,
  "trigger_metrics": ["entropy_delta","kv_norm"],
  "entropy_threshold": 0.25
}
```

Maria P.: nice. ops considerations: runtime must expose a clear contract: when we say "precision changed at token T", the client-facing sequence must remain deterministic for replay and eval. also trace points for observability.

ops-bot: New note: canary quota required for runtime-sliced precision feature. Please coordinate with eng-sre for a reserved pool. :white_check_mark:

Chris W.: rollback plan: default to the non-gradient path per-endpoint flag. also telemetry events: (endpoint, model, switch_point, pre_entropy, post_entropy, latency_delta). we need these to evaluate cost vs quality.

Liam T.: question about KV serialization: if we store KV per-precision variant, memory blows up. idea: store canonical high-fidelity kv (FP16) and lazily cast to lower precision when serving. cost: cast on hot path but saves storage. thoughts?

Sasha R.: lazy-cast seems pragmatic. cast latency measured ~0.4ms per layer on our test GPU for typical layer sizes. acceptable if we batch casts. we should also benchmark end-to-end for long sequences.

Maria P.: action items: 1) Sasha + Liam to run an A/B perf+quality experiment using block-aligned precision-gradient and lazy-cast KV by EOD next week. 2) Chris to draft the runtime contract + telemetry fields. 3) Ops: reserve a small canary pool (ops-bot already pinged eng-sre).

Sasha R.: logging one caveat — some ops (rotary/rope hooks) behave subtly under 4bit; we should add a small test matrix for positional encodings.

Maria P.: noted. thanks all. if results look promising we'll fold into the quant profile API (separate opt-in flag). :thumbsup:
